scene.note: Tonight's count sits at the top of kit_store.py, your variables keep and change it, and the terminal shows the result.

steps.note: Dougie wants the team's name kept under one name, so nobody types it again.
Under Task 1 a variable stores the name as text, in quotes.
Printing the variable shows the text it holds.
Dougie's count arrives at the top of the file as two named numbers.
Under Task 2 a new variable starts with the number of ropes in the store.
The terminal shows the count after its label, with one space between them.
Some ropes went out on tonight's callout.
Under Task 3 the same variable gets a new value: what is left in the store.
The terminal now shows two counts, before and after the callout.
Two variables called x and y hold the names of two people on the team.
Each gets a name that says what it holds, everywhere it appears.
The file prints the same two lines as before, and now Dougie can read it.
